reviewer: independent subagent; fresh-open inspection, source comparison, node-link inspection, and four review renders
rubric: AGENT.md, five criteria at 2 points each

evidence: Purdue BoilerLink's current AEPi page lists 1051 David Ross Road; its searchable page content was available on review date 2026-10-26.
Official Purdue GIS FID 754 also lists 1051 David Ross Road, and the project's saved satellite overlay aligns its polygon with a visible roof.
The same GIS feature's BUILDING_N label is Chi Phi, so address/roof correspondence does not conclusively resolve current occupancy.
GIS FID 821 is a separate Alpha Epsilon Pi candidate at 116 Fowler Avenue and is documented as not used for this model.
findings: The current official address and GIS/address match support the selected footprint, but the official GIS name conflict and absence of recent direct occupancy evidence remain unresolved.

evidence: Fresh-open geometry compares all 60 selected foundation ring vertices to GIS FID 754; maximum corresponding XY error is 1.11e-06 m.
The local coordinate transform and foundation ring preserve the source plan outline and its orientation rather than scaling to an unrelated bounding box.
findings: The sub-millimetre comparison is to the GIS polygon transformed into the project frame; it does not establish the GIS roof/wall edge or survey accuracy.

evidence: The attributed 2009 Purdue AEPi photograph supports a three-visible-story brick house with a mansard roof and dormer cues; it is historical style evidence only.
Fresh-open bounds reach 13.57 m; wall and roof components are separately modeled, with the chimney cap reaching 13.57 m.
No surveyed elevation or current roof-height source was supplied; wall levels, roof breaks, dormers, chimney and total height remain estimates.
findings: Retain explicit estimated status for floor heights and roof geometry until a current elevation, measured plan, or suitably classified LiDAR surface is available.

evidence: The revised exterior preview now reads as horizontal red masonry at the saved camera distance; independent fresh-open node inspection confirms UV coordinates feed the Brick Texture, its color feeds Principled Base Color, and its factor drives bump relief.
Fresh-open object-name inspection found 30 facade window fronts, 20 AC units, 9 dormer glazing objects and 36 entrance-related objects.

Fresh Blender renders from front, east, west and rear show fenestrated side/rear elevations and the mansard silhouette; exposed internal/recessed faces remain comparatively plain and are not supported by a current elevation.

The visible entry, Greek-letter sign, projecting window treatments, dark shingle roof and masonry match the broad historic-photo cues, while exact bay/window rhythm and current materials remain unverified.
findings: The key revision-1 defect (brick appearing as vertical siding) is corrected. Side/rear details and exposed recessed surfaces remain schematic because current target-facing imagery and measured elevations are unavailable.

evidence: An independent Blender 5.2.3 process reopened the exact candidate SHA256 8074f7c27f1b0ba25e0699f056db21611249679335d2796a035db4b40673a961 and found the expected scene, stable asset collection and local-coordinate flag.
The collection contains 710 objects (708 meshes) and 20 referenced materials; missing-material meshes, mesh-parent errors and unpacked external images are all zero.

The audit includes current-address/GIS records, the geometry transform, fresh-open probe, exterior/interior views and four independent review renders; the asset has 155 named representative interior objects.
The interior is still illustrative rather than tied to a public floor plan, and this standalone grade does not establish integration into the campus master.
findings: The model is portable and its evidence is organized; confirm and document master integration separately. Interior room positions remain representative estimates.
